catalog_quote: Stress is partly conditioned by word-class; there is a ‘basic’ stress pattern found in nouns, adjectives and some types of verbs. There is also a ‘special verbal pattern’, found with ‘ambifixing verbs’ ... and ‘positional verbs’ ... In this second pattern, stress placement is sensitive to three main factors: (i) a light–heavy contrast in syllable nuclei, where light nuclei are those filled by /ɪ/ or the epenthetic vowels [ɪ ə] and everything else is heavy; (ii) word-structure ...; (iii) morphological structure (in verbs) ... It is ultimately possible to predict stress placement from interactions of these factors. ... Basic stress pattern The basic pattern is to stress the initial syllable, such as [ˈa.ra.ˌɡab] ‘sea’, [ˈka.nam] ‘snake’, [ˈkaŋ.ɡa] ‘bridge’ ... [ˈse.le.mi] ‘clothes’. ...
